### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4e3dcc6e4c46d6b14ba832a838e4dab3cdec33e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6ddfa252c563e720e2f2e41f15ec371746ea1003` — the merge of head `9754555cc8cc8bfe01b56cc2155f25e8aa5795d5` into base `d4e3dcc6e4c46d6b14ba832a838e4dab3cdec33e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6ddfa252c563e720e2f2e41f15ec371746ea1003 && git checkout 6ddfa252c563e720e2f2e41f15ec371746ea1003
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4e3dcc6e4c46d6b14ba832a838e4dab3cdec33e 9754555cc8cc8bfe01b56cc2155f25e8aa5795d5 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4e3dcc6e4c46d6b14ba832a838e4dab3cdec33e && git merge --no-ff 9754555cc8cc8bfe01b56cc2155f25e8aa5795d5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4e3dcc6e4c46d6b14ba832a838e4dab3cdec33e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Part of #32670. Item ③ of review 6882047833 on #33361 (the separate, declared move owed once #32354 landed; it landed in #33405) plus #33361 nit N1. Only `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts`, its test file and one patch changeset. `servedBundleAddressOf` now picks the address by served-holder count on the protocol read: one served holder reads the environment-wide list, two or more read the answering holder's own address. The registry-only read keeps the per-holder address (`listItems` still lists a disabled holder's dependent addition; ablation 2 shows the leak if forced). N1: the unreachable environment-item branch returns `NO_BUNDLE`. Probe: 12 of 1,152 answers move, all toward the world where the disabled holder holds nothing (protocol read, BETA disabled, fr-FR, the pair's row → the dependent's addition). The PR declares no `!`; please rule the Clause-② arm for those 12 moved answers. plugin-email 1018/1018; ablation 1 (main loader) 2 red, ablation 2 6 red. Not measured locally: teardown-shape --self-test, dual-build-cjs-loads, type-check-debt (CI covers).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `9754555cc8cc8bfe01b56cc2155f25e8aa5795d5`
Local-runs: none

The PR's file list is `.changeset/32670-email-send-served-count.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts` and `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.test.ts`. It has no published schema and no governed path, and on my ruling below it has no narrowing. So this is a plain review record with no ④. The change was read at `7612a59d`. The head adds only a merge of `origin/main` that touches no `plugin-email` file.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The new rule is correct.** `servedBundleAddressOf` is reached only when `served.length < holders.length`. Over the protocol (`servedCountDecides`), `onServedCount` now returns the environment-wide address (`undefined`) when fewer than 2 holders are served, and the holder's own address otherwise. That is exactly what `bundleAddressOf`'s nothing-disabled branch does on the holder count (`holders.length < 2 → undefined`). So when exactly one holder is served, the disabled branch now reads the same list the one-holder world reads. Since #33405 (#32354) that list holds none of the disabled holder's members. Its own items, its pair's rows and a dependent's addition are all withheld, so the read equals the world where the disabled package holds nothing (ABSENT). With two or more served holders the address is the holder's own, as before. With no protocol (`servedCountDecides` false) nothing changes.
- **The built-ins re-resolve.** This is the auth name with its only holder disabled, which takes the `served.length = 0` branch. The address moves from the built-ins' own address to the environment-wide list, and every answer stays the same: the pinned `an auth name one package overrides, ALPHA disabled` protocol row is unchanged on both orders.
- **N1.** The `resolved.holder.kind !== 'package'` branch now returns `NO_BUNDLE`. It sits inside the disabled branch, where the name has a package holder. `getEnvironmentScopedItem` binds an environment item for a held name to that holder's slot (`compositeHoldersOf` / `overlaySlotBinding`), so it answers none, and the branch stays unreachable. Even if it were reachable, `NO_BUNDLE` is the row-37 answer ruled in 6882047833 ④, not a new refusal. No answer moves.
- **The 12 moved answers.** All are on the protocol read, in the state `two holders, BETA disabled`, at fr-FR, for the callers omitted, null, ALPHA, BOTH, VIA_ALPHA and ADDER in both orders. Each goes from `PAIR fr-FR` to `ADDER fr-FR`. Both sides are served templates: no answer becomes a refusal, no refusal changes, and the BETA, NEITHER and BUILTIN cells are unchanged. The new answer is the ABSENT answer and also main's answer for a name one package holds (the CONTROL), which is #33361's R4-F shape and not a rule this PR adds.
- **Pins exist for every moved answer.** The `two holders, BETA disabled` protocol expectations move for exactly those six callers × 2 orders. The new `one holder` CONTROL (4 tests) pins the equality. The author's ablation 1 (main's loader) turns both orders red, and ablation 2 shows why the registry read keeps the per-holder address.
- **Emitters of codes named in the text.** The only refusal named is `409 outside-closure` (`EmailTemplateAmbiguousError`, both throw sites in `servedBundleAddressOf` unchanged). `NO_BUNDLE` is a module-private symbol that renders as `no template` (`readBundle` returns `[]`). No new code is emitted.

### ② Semver level

**Clause-② ruling: `no`, as declared.** No request that was served before is refused now. The 12 moves are served → served. They re-address the read to the list that holds what the name holds once the disabled package holds nothing (ADR-0150 D3), which is the answer the same world gives with BETA absent. This is the #33587 shape (one outcome's value corrected), not #33383's (a 200 becomes a 404). So it gets no `!`, no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker.

**`Metadata-protocol: none` stands.** Nothing an author writes is refused, and nothing changes meaning: the pair row still binds ALPHA's fr-FR slot, and its precedence against a dependent's addition is main's existing one-holder rule (the same reasoning as #33383's ruling).

`@objectstack/plugin-email: patch`. The changeset carries both declaration lines and a FROM → TO paragraph that matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Scope holds: only `plugin-email`. The `_env` cell of #32183 row 17 (#33385, area E1) and the R4-G flow doors stay out, as `Part of #32670` says.
- The acceptance note's registry-only disabled-versus-absent gap (`no template` against `ADDER fr-FR`) is a declared residual. It needs `listItems` to withhold a disabled holder's side, which belongs to a separate door.
- nit (accepted): the auth-name address move (built-ins' own address → environment-wide) is pinned only by its answers, not by the request's `packageId`. Answer pins are the contract, so this is no defect.

- The PR is a draft, opened by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` for the seat.
